title: Parity
summary: Integer parity defines the predicates even and odd by divisibility by two.

context.framework: integers with ordinary addition and multiplication
context.note: Revision 3 separates the definitions from the distinct classification theorem that every integer has exactly one parity.

assumptions.text: The integer structure with its ordinary arithmetic is fixed.

content.plain: An integer is even when it is twice an integer and odd when it is one more than twice an integer.
content.exact: For n∈Z, Even(n) iff there exists k∈Z with n=2·k; Odd(n) iff there exists k∈Z with n=2·k+1. Exhaustiveness and exclusivity are separate theorems, not part of these definitions.
content.example: 18 is even because 18=2·9. 19 is odd because 19=2·9+1.
content.caveat: The theorem that every integer is exactly one of even or odd requires the division algorithm or an equivalent arithmetic argument.

relations.note: Congruence modulo two induces the two parity classes after the classification theorem is established.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Stops an unproved classification theorem from being smuggled into a definition record. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
